meta.name: Geriatric Fall — Hip Fragility Fracture on Anticoagulation

patient.name: Eleanor Voss
patient.chiefComplaint: Right hip pain after a ground-level fall, unable to bear weight

history.hpi: Home health aide arrived for a scheduled visit and found the patient on the kitchen floor. Patient reports tripping over a throw rug approximately 20 minutes prior; denies loss of consciousness, denies striking her head. Complains of severe right hip pain, unable to stand or bear weight.
history.lastOralIntake: Breakfast approximately 2 hours prior to the fall
history.events: Home health aide found patient on the kitchen floor and called 911; fall was unwitnessed but patient is able to describe the mechanism

scene.dispatch: 89-year-old female, fall, conscious and breathing, residence
scene.location: Single-story home, kitchen, patient supine on tile floor near a throw rug
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted; throw rug identified as fall hazard
scene.bystanders: Home health aide present, found the patient and called 911
visualCues: Right leg visibly shortened and externally rotated
Throw rug bunched near the patient
Medication organizer visible on counter with an apixaban blister pack

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find an 89-year-old female supine on the kitchen floor with obvious right leg deformity. She is alert, in visible pain, and denies head strike.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin pale and cool
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact bilaterally in upper extremities and left leg; unable to assess right leg due to pain
otherFindings: Right hip pain 8/10, worse with any attempted movement
Right leg shortened and externally rotated
Mild baseline confusion consistent with known dementia per aide
Denies head strike, denies neck or back pain
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so much, please don't move it."

transitions.if: Primary survey and pain management completed
transitions.condition: Crew performs a MARCH primary survey, identifies apixaban use during history-taking, splints the deformed right hip in the position found, and provides analgesia before further movement.

phases.name: Primary survey and pain management completed
phases.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, obtains a medication history revealing apixaban use, assesses neurovascular status of the injured leg, splints in position found, and administers weight-based fentanyl with cautious dosing given her age and anticoagulant therapy.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming no immediate life threats on primary survey, the crew identifies apixaban use during history-taking, splints the deformed right hip in the position found, and provides analgesia before further movement.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and pedal pulses present bilaterally, distal right foot warm with brisk capillary refill
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to right hip; strength intact in all other extremities
otherFindings: No midline spinal tenderness on palpation

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey; rule out life threats before focusing on the hip
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out life threats before focusing on the obvious deformity.

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain medication history; identify apixaban (anticoagulant) use
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Obtain medical history from patient or family including: Allergies Medications Past medical and surgical history Last meal Events leading up to the injury
expectedActions.rationale: Anticoagulant use significantly raises the risk of occult hemorrhage and must drive later reassessment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess pallor, pulse, capillary refill, sensation, and movement of right leg before splinting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Vascular status of extremity: Pallor Pulse Capillary refill and skin temperature. Neurologic status of extremity: Sensation to light touch Distal movement of extremity
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a neurovascular baseline before and after splinting to detect compromise.

expectedActions.shortAction: Splint right hip/leg in position found before any further movement
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Strongly consider pain management before attempting to move a suspected fracture. Use splints as appropriate to limit movement of suspected fracture
expectedActions.rationale: Splinting in position found minimizes pain and further tissue damage.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 55 mcg IV (55 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate analgesia before splinting and transport reduces pain and physiologic stress.

expectedActions.shortAction: Titrate opioid cautiously; monitor for hypoventilation given her comorbidities
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: To reduce the risk of adverse effects like respiratory depression, use opioids with caution and judicious dosing in patients with comorbid conditions, beginning with lower doses and gradually increasing based on response
expectedActions.rationale: Elderly patients with polypharmacy are at higher risk for opioid-related respiratory depression.

transitions.if: Splinted, medicated, transported with serial monitoring
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes the bleeding risk conferred by apixaban and continues serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment en route.

transitions.if: Anticoagulant use not identified, serial monitoring omitted
transitions.condition: Crew splints and medicates the hip but never obtains a medication history, missing the apixaban use; serial reassessment is skipped en route as a result.

phases.name: Splinted, medicated, transported with serial monitoring
phases.description: Patient is packaged with a splinted right hip, pain well controlled, and transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment given her anticoagulant use and elevated risk for occult hemorrhage.
phases.triggerCondition: After splinting and analgesia, the crew recognizes the bleeding risk conferred by apixaban and continues serial reassessment en route to detect early signs of occult hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and pedal pulses present bilaterally, skin warming
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to right hip; strength intact in all other extremities
otherFindings: Pain improved to 2/10 with splinting and analgesia
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel much better now, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and neuro status serially en route; monitor for occult hemorrhage
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor patient for deterioration over time with serial vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and repeat neurologic status assessment
expectedActions.rationale: Anticoagulated geriatric patients can develop occult hemorrhage without early hypotension.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to appropriate trauma-capable facility per field triage guideline
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Decisions regarding transport destination should be based on the ACS-COT 2022 National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients
expectedActions.rationale: Ensures the patient reaches a facility capable of managing a geriatric hip fracture with anticoagulation.

phases.name: Anticoagulant use not identified, serial monitoring omitted
phases.description: The crew splints and medicates the hip but never asks about medications, missing the apixaban history. Without recognizing the bleeding risk, serial reassessment is skipped en route, and the patient develops evolving hemorrhagic shock without early warning signs.
phases.triggerCondition: Medication history is not obtained during the secondary assessment, so the crew is unaware of apixaban use. Serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment is skipped en route; the patient develops progressive hypotension from occult hemorrhage before it is recognized.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready, delayed capillary refill
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to right hip at this time
otherFindings: No repeat vital signs obtained since the scene

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize occult hemorrhagic shock; establish IV access and initiate fluid bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients with compensated shock may not manifest hypotension until severe blood loss has occurred
expectedActions.rationale: Anticoagulated patients can decompensate rapidly once hypotension appears, since compensatory mechanisms mask early blood loss.
